title: How does a sewing machine join two threads to make a stitch?
answer: A common sewing machine uses one thread from above and another from a small spool below the cloth. The needle carries the upper thread down and then starts back up, leaving a loop. A part under the cloth catches that loop and passes it around the lower spool, linking the two threads. The upper thread pulls tight and the cloth shifts a little before the next stitch.
facts: The small spool under the cloth is called a bobbin.

title: How does a rice cooker notice when the water is nearly gone?
answer: A rice cooker can watch the temperature of its pot. While water is boiling, it takes in a lot of heat as some of it turns to steam. As the rice takes up water and steam escapes, there is less free water left. The bottom of the pot can then get hotter more quickly. The cooker can use that change to lower the heat or stop cooking.

facts: An electric rice cooker can use more than one temperature sensor to track cooking.

title: How does a can opener run its little cutting wheel around a can?
answer: A hand can opener can have two small wheels near each other. The rough wheel grips the rim of the can. The sharp wheel reaches the part it will cut. Turning the handle moves the rough wheel, which helps feed the can past the sharp one. The cut follows the rim as the can moves. Designs differ in where they cut and what edge they leave.
facts: On many hand openers, squeezing two handles brings the wheels together around the rim.

title: Why can a bottle opener lift a cap with a small push?
answer: A metal crown cap has bent edges that grip the bottle’s rim. A bottle opener can slip an edge under one side of the cap while another part of the opener rests against it. When the handle moves, the opener turns around its resting point and lifts part of the cap. The bend frees enough of the edge for the cap to come away.
aliases: how does bottle opener open cap
facts: A crown cap is named for its ring of small ridges around the edge.

title: How do kitchen tongs pinch food without touching it with your hands?
answer: A common pair of kitchen tongs has two long arms joined at one end. The ends far from the join can grip a piece of food. Squeezing the handles brings those gripping ends together. When you loosen your hand, a spring can open the arms again. The long arms mean you can reach something in a pan while keeping your hand farther from the hot surface.
facts: Some tongs have rounded gripping ends, while others have ridges that help hold slippery food.

title: Why does twisting an ice tray make the cubes come out?
answer: Water freezes inside the little pockets of an ice tray and takes their shape. In a flexible tray, a gentle twist changes the shape of those pockets a little. The solid cubes cannot bend to match the new shape the way the tray does. Some of their contact with the tray breaks, so the cubes can drop out when the tray is turned over.
facts: A soft-bottomed tray can also bend at the bottom of just one pocket to release a cube.

title: Why do some doors close slowly on their own?
answer: Some doors have a little box and an arm that move together as the door opens. Opening the door presses on a spring inside the box. The spring pushes back to close the door. In many designs, closing also makes oil move through a narrow opening inside the box. The slow-moving oil helps keep the arm from letting the door swing shut all at once.
facts: A closer combines a part that moves the door with another part that slows the motion down.
